title: U.S. House, District 12
counties: Hillsborough (part, per 2026 reporting on redrawn district)
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 12th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: WUSF (Aug 12 and Aug 18, 2026) and Florida Politics report the November ballot is incumbent Gus Bilirakis (R), Democratic primary winner Kimberly Overman and no-party candidate Branden Schivener (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-08-18/pasco-primary-results-2026-kimberly-overman-wins-primary-setting-up-face-off-against-us-rep-gus-bilirakis ; https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-08-12/democrats-face-uphill-battle-quest-to-wrest-the-seat-held-by-congressman-gus-bilirakis ; https://floridapolitics.com/archives/815521-despite-financial-disadvantage-kimberly-overman-wins-democratic-primary-to-face-gus-bilirakis-in-cd-12/). Write-in candidates not confirmed. Florida's Legislature passed a new congressional map in the April 2026 special session (Senate vote 21-17 on April 29, 2026) and the Florida Supreme Court on June 10, 2026 declined (6-1) to block it, so the new district lines apply to the Nov. 3, 2026 election; litigation on the merits continues. (https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/04/29/florida-legislature-passes-desantis-congressional-redistricting-map/; https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2026/06/10/florida-supreme-court-clears-way-for-new-redistricting-map-in-2026; https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-06-11/florida-supreme-court-rejects-challenge-new-redistricting-map) County list reflects pre-2026 district boundaries unless a 2026 source is cited; boundaries changed under the April 2026 map and the exact new county composition was not confirmed in searches run for this guide. NOTE ON NAME SPELLING: the no-party candidate's own campaign site (https://brandenscrivenerfl.info/) and Ballotpedia (https://ballotpedia.org/Florida's_12th_Congressional_District_election,_2026) spell his name 'Branden Scrivener'; WUSF's report used 'Schivener'. Confirm the ballot spelling with the Division of Elections.

candidates.name: Gus Bilirakis
candidates.residence: Palm Harbor, Pinellas County (per prior reporting; not re-verified)
candidates.background: Gus Bilirakis, an attorney and former state House member, has served in the U.S. House since 2007, succeeding his father Michael Bilirakis. He sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee, where he leads the consumer-protection subcommittee and serves on the health and communications subcommittees. He had no Republican primary opponent in 2026 and advanced directly to the November general election in the redrawn 12th District, seeking an 11th term.
candidates.primary_result: No Republican primary; advanced automatically to Nov 3 general election (WUSF: https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-08-12/democrats-face-uphill-battle-quest-to-wrest-the-seat-held-by-congressman-gus-bilirakis)

taxes.summary: Bilirakis voted for H.R. 1 (the 2025 reconciliation law), which extended the 2017 individual tax cuts and added new deductions while reducing projected federal spending on Medicaid and SNAP. No separate statement on the tradeoff was found. He has also backed eliminating or reducing taxes on overtime, tips and Social Security benefits.

candidates.name: Kimberly Overman
candidates.occupation: Certified financial planner; former Hillsborough County commissioner
candidates.residence: Tampa area, Hillsborough County (per Hoodline; not re-verified)
candidates.background: Kimberly Overman is a certified financial planner and small-business owner who served on the Hillsborough County Commission from 2018 to 2022. She says her approach is grounded in decades of public service and the realities of working-class life, including a period of housing insecurity. She won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.7% over Darren McAuley, a physician and Florida Air National Guard state air surgeon who spent nearly four times as much on the race.
